title: Langhede and Thomassen's exponential correspondence-colouring conjecture for planar graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. A **correspondence assignment** $(L,M)$ for $G$ consists of a list assignment $L$ and, for each edge, a partial matching between the corresponding vertex-colour pairs; an $(L,M)$-colouring chooses a colour from each list while avoiding matched pairs on every edge. The class of planar graphs has exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings if there exists a constant $c>0$ such that every planar graph $G$ and every $5$-correspondence assignment $(L,M)$ admit at least $2^{c\cdot v(G)}$ distinct $(L,M)$-colourings.

**Langhede and Thomassen's conjecture.** Planar graphs have exponentially many $5$-correspondence colourings.

This conjecture asks for an exponential strengthening of the known $5$-correspondence-colourability of planar graphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Luke Postle and Evelyne Smith-Roberge, “Exponentially Many Correspondence Colourings of Planar and Locally Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2309.17291 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17291

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).
